The model refuses to run without an internet connection on the user's own device
A user's crafted input causes the assistant to ignore its scope and leak internal information
The model's answers are identical every time for the same input, which users find repetitive
The model learns from each conversation and changes its own weights overnight

explanation: Correct: A and C. Hallucinated content and prompt injection are two of the central failure modes of LLM systems and each needs a mitigation on the register. B describes a hosted service in a confused way. D is not how sampled outputs behave and is not a risk. E is false: inference does not update the model's weights.

prompt: During discovery, a client's sponsor insists the assistant must be "100% accurate" before it can go live. What is the architect's most effective response?

options.text: Agree to the target and plan to keep testing until no further errors can be found in the test set
Explain that probabilistic systems have an error rate, then agree accuracy targets per use case and controls
Decline the engagement, since a requirement of perfect accuracy cannot be met by any system and the sponsor will not budge
Promise the target now and renegotiate once the system is built and the real numbers are known

explanation: Correct: B. Expectation alignment means being honest about the nature of the system and turning an impossible absolute into a measurable target plus controls for the residual risk. A sets up a failure at launch. C abandons a solvable conversation. D damages trust when the renegotiation comes.

prompt: A client opens an engagement with "we want an AI agent for our warehouse". Before proposing any architecture, what should the architect do first?

options.text: Draft a proposal for a multi-agent warehouse system based on common patterns seen across the industry
Build a quick prototype agent to show the client what is technically possible today
Run structured discovery: interview the people, map the process, find the problems and measures
Ask the client which model they would prefer to use so that the design can be sized around it

explanation: Correct: C. A vague request needs structured discovery before design: who is affected, what the process looks like today, what hurts, and how success will be measured. A and B commit to a solution before the problem is understood. D asks an implementation question at the wrong time.

prompt: A finance director instructs the team to use the cheapest model for a document-analysis solution that feeds regulatory filings. Testing shows the cheapest model has a materially higher error rate on this task. What should the architect do?

options.text: Present the error rates, cost difference and filing consequences, recommend the model that meets the bar
Comply with the instruction, since budget decisions belong to the finance director and not to the architect or the team
Quietly use the more capable model and absorb the extra cost in another budget line to avoid conflict
Escalate to the finance director's manager and ask for the instruction to be overruled on quality grounds

explanation: Correct: A. Communicating a trade-off means putting the evidence and consequences in front of the decision-maker and making a clear recommendation; the business then owns the choice. B hides a material risk. C is dishonest and will surface later. D jumps the stakeholder before the evidence has been presented to them.

prompt: A stakeholder demands complete answers in under one second from an assistant that performs multi-step retrieval and reasoning. Engineering analysis shows the pipeline cannot finish in under three seconds. Which approach best manages this?

options.text: Accept the one-second target and hope that the model provider's latency improves before launch
Remove the retrieval step so that the target can be met, and accept the lower accuracy that results from it
Ignore the demand, since it is technically unreasonable and will be forgotten once the system ships
Share the analysis, offer options such as streaming or a simpler fast mode, and agree an SLA

explanation: Correct: D. Managing an SLA expectation means showing the evidence, explaining the trade-off, and offering concrete alternatives that preserve what the stakeholder actually values, then agreeing a measurable target. A sets up a missed commitment. B trades away quality without discussion. C leaves the stakeholder uninformed and unaligned.

prompt: A consultancy is handing a completed assistant to the client's own engineers, who will run it from now on. Beyond the source code, which set of artefacts matters most for a successful handoff?

options.text: The sales proposal and the original statement of work that defined the engagement's scope
The chat transcripts the consultancy's team used with their AI tools while building the system over the engagement
A recording of the final demo and the slide deck that was presented to the steering committee
Architecture docs with decision records, runbooks, the evaluation suite, and a prompt-iteration guide

explanation: Correct: D. A team that will operate and evolve the system needs to know how it is built and why, how to run and recover it, how to tell whether a change made it better, and how to change prompts without regressing. A, B and C are historical artefacts that do not help anyone operate or improve the system.

prompt: Three months after launch, the sponsor's interest in an assistant is fading. The fortnightly report lists token spend, latency and uptime, and nothing else. What change would most improve alignment?

options.text: Report business outcomes the sponsor cares about, such as cases resolved and hours saved, with the technical metrics
Send the report every week instead of every fortnight so that the sponsor hears from the team more often and stays engaged
Add more technical metrics such as cache hit rate, p99 latency and error budgets to the existing report
Stop sending written reports and schedule a quarterly review meeting with the sponsor instead

explanation: Correct: A. Stakeholder feedback loops stay healthy when the reporting speaks to the outcomes the sponsor signed up for; technical metrics alone show cost without value. B and C send more of the same. D reduces contact instead of fixing its content.

prompt: Which lifecycle phase does this activity belong to: interviewing claims handlers to learn how claims are triaged today and where delays occur?

options.text: Design
Handoff
Monitoring
Discovery

explanation: Correct: D. Learning how the work is done today and where it hurts is discovery, which comes before any solution is designed. A would be choosing patterns and components. B is the transfer of a finished system to its operators. C is observing a system in production.

prompt: Which lifecycle phase does this activity belong to: reviewing a month of production evaluation results and choosing the next set of prompt changes to make?

options.text: Iteration
Discovery
Handoff
Design

explanation: Correct: A. Using production evidence to decide the next improvements is iteration, the phase that follows monitoring and keeps the system improving after launch. B is understanding the problem before building. C is transferring ownership. D is choosing the architecture before it is built.

prompt: An architect must explain to a non-technical steering committee why the team chose retrieval over fine-tuning for a policy assistant. Which way of communicating the decision is most effective?

options.text: Walk the committee through the embedding model benchmarks and the vector index configuration in detail, with slides
State the decision only, since the committee does not need to understand the technical reasoning
Frame it in the committee's terms, such as speed of policy updates, cost and auditability, and record the trade-offs
Send the committee the technical design document and invite any questions they may have by email

explanation: Correct: C. Communicating an architectural decision means translating it into the audience's terms (currency of information, cost, traceability) and leaving a written record of the options and trade-offs. A buries the committee in detail they cannot act on. B denies them the reasoning they need to support the choice. D delegates the explanation to a document written for engineers.

prompt: A team is writing the architecture documentation for a Claude solution that other engineers will implement. Which content is most important to include so that implementation stays faithful to the design?

options.text: A list of every library version the design team happened to have installed on their own laptops
The components, data flows including sensitive data, prompts and owners, evaluation gates, and decision rationale
A copy of the model provider's public documentation on the API, models and prompt engineering
A narrative of the project's history, the people involved and the meetings at which the key decisions were taken

explanation: Correct: B. Implementation guidance needs the structure, the data flows (especially for sensitive data), the prompts as first-class artefacts, the quality gates and the rationale that stops implementers from undoing decisions. A is environment trivia. C is available to everyone already. D is context, not guidance.

prompt: An architect is closing the discovery phase of a new engagement. Which TWO outputs are the most important to have agreed in writing before design begins? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The problem statement with success criteria and how they will be measured
The final version of the system prompt that the assistant will use in production
The constraints: data sensitivity, compliance obligations, integration points and non-functional targets
The chosen vector database and the configuration it will run with in production
The colour palette and typography for the user interface the assistant will be presented in

explanation: Correct: A and C. Discovery should end with an agreed problem and measure of success, plus the constraints the design must honour; without those, design decisions have nothing to be checked against. B and D are design and implementation outputs. E is a presentation detail.

prompt: Midway through a build, stakeholders keep adding requests: new data sources, extra user groups, more output formats. Which TWO practices best manage this while keeping the relationship healthy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Accept every request immediately so that the stakeholders stay happy and engaged with the project
Log each request against the agreed scope and show its cost, timeline and risk impact before accepting
Refuse all changes until the original scope has shipped, then revisit the backlog of requests
Hold a regular prioritisation session where stakeholders trade new requests off against commitments
Stop reporting progress so that the stakeholders have less to react to and fewer ideas for additions

explanation: Correct: B and D. Scope is managed by making the impact of each change visible against the agreed baseline and by giving stakeholders a structured forum to prioritise. A guarantees overrun. C damages the relationship and ignores legitimate change. E breaks the feedback loop.

prompt: An assistant has been in production for six months. Which TWO activities belong to the monitoring and iteration phases of its lifecycle? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Tracking accuracy, latency, cost and safety against the agreed targets and alerting on drift
Interviewing stakeholders to decide whether the project should exist and what problem it would solve
Feeding reviewed production failures into the evaluation set and shipping prompt updates through the gate
Choosing between a workflow and an agent architecture for the assistant's core processing loop
Writing the first version of the runbook for the operations team that will take the system over

explanation: Correct: A and C. Monitoring watches the live metrics and catches drift; iteration turns what monitoring finds into evaluated improvements. B is discovery. D is design. E is handoff preparation.

prompt: A sponsor asks the architect to commit to a response-time SLA for an assistant that is still being designed. What is the right way to handle the request?

options.text: Commit to a one-second SLA, because that is what the sponsor wants to hear and is prepared to fund the project for
Refuse to discuss SLAs at all until the system has been running in production for a while
Commit to the same SLA as the company's existing web services, since users expect parity
Propose a provisional target from prototype measurements, define the measure, and confirm after load testing

explanation: Correct: D. SLA alignment is evidence-based and staged: a provisional, measured target with a clear definition and a point at which it becomes firm. A commits without evidence. B leaves the sponsor without anything to plan around. C borrows a number from systems with different characteristics.

prompt: An engineering lead is rolling out Claude Code to a 40-person team. Early adopters have each configured it differently, producing inconsistent code style and repeated setup effort. What is the most effective enablement step?

options.text: Let each engineer keep their own configuration, since personal preference is what drives adoption
Restrict the tool to the three most experienced engineers until standards emerge from their practice and can be written down
Write a one-page memo asking everyone to configure the tool consistently and follow the house style
Commit shared project configuration: an instructions file with conventions and commands, plus permission settings

explanation: Correct: D. Team-level configuration lives in the repository so every engineer, and the tool, starts from the same conventions, commands and permissions; it is versioned and reviewed like code. A preserves the inconsistency. B slows adoption without creating a standard. C relies on memory rather than configuration.

prompt: A team uses one AI coding session to both write a change and review it. Reviews rarely find anything, yet defects keep reaching production. Which adjustment most directly improves review quality?

options.text: Review in a separate session that has not seen the authoring context, with a checklist and a human on the merge
Ask the same session to review more carefully and to list at least five issues before it may approve
Stop using AI for reviews altogether and rely on the existing automated test suite to catch defects
Lower the bar for merging so that reviews are quicker and the team can ship fixes faster when defects do reach production

explanation: Correct: A. A reviewer that shares the author's context inherits the author's assumptions; isolating the review context and giving it explicit criteria restores an independent check, with a human still accountable for the merge. B forces findings rather than finding them. C discards a useful tool instead of fixing how it is used. D makes the defect problem worse.

prompt: A production agent has started taking unexpected actions on a subset of requests. The on-call engineer wants to rewrite the system prompt immediately. What should happen first?

options.text: Rewrite the system prompt as proposed, since the prompt is the most likely cause of a behaviour change
Pull the traces for the affected requests to see what preceded the actions, and contain the blast radius
Roll back to the previous model version without further investigation, since the model is the likely cause
Disable the agent permanently and open a project to rebuild it from scratch with stricter controls

explanation: Correct: B. Operational issue resolution starts with evidence: the traces show what the agent actually saw and did, which separates a prompt problem from injected content, a bad tool result or a data change; containment comes alongside, not after. A changes the system before the cause is known. C guesses at a different cause. D is disproportionate for a subset of requests.

prompt: A developer repeatedly types the same twenty-line explanation of the project's test commands, directory layout and coding conventions at the start of every Claude Code session. What should they do instead?

options.text: Put it in the project's committed instructions file so every session loads it and the team shares it
Keep pasting it each time, since fresh instructions at the start of a session are more reliable
Paste it into the first file of the codebase as a block comment so the tool encounters it while reading
Ask the tool to remember it in its own hidden personal settings so nobody else needs to see it

explanation: Correct: A. Project instructions that every session needs belong in the project's committed instructions file, where the tool picks them up automatically and the team maintains them together. B wastes effort and drifts. C hides configuration in an unrelated file. D keeps shared knowledge personal.

prompt: A team wants AI-assisted coding to speed up routine work without letting unreviewed changes reach the main branch. Which workflow change achieves this?

options.text: Give the coding assistant permission to push directly to main so that it can work without waiting for anyone
Allow the assistant to run only inside a sandbox with no access to the repository or its history
Let the assistant open branches and pull requests that run CI and need a human review to merge
Require a human to type every line the assistant suggests so that nothing is committed unread

explanation: Correct: C. The productive pattern keeps the assistant inside the existing safety net: branches, automated checks and human-reviewed merges, so speed comes without bypassing review. A removes the safety net. B removes the usefulness. D removes the speed.

prompt: An engineer debugging a failing Claude integration sees the model returning malformed JSON in roughly one response in fifty. Which approach resolves this most robustly?

options.text: Add "please return valid JSON" to the prompt and consider the issue fixed once the next few responses parse correctly
Constrain the output with a schema (such as a tool definition), validate in code, and retry or fall back
Parse whatever comes back with a lenient parser and silently ignore any response that fails to parse
Switch to a different model each time a malformed response appears so that no single model is relied on

explanation: Correct: B. Structured output is made reliable by constraining it to a schema and then validating in code, with a defined retry or fallback path for the rare miss. A lowers the rate but leaves the failure unhandled. C silently drops data. D adds variability without addressing the handling.

prompt: A platform team wants to scale AI-assisted development across the organisation without adding operational risk. Which TWO practices best support this? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Standard, versioned project configurations and permission settings that teams start from
Allowing each team to grant the assistant any permission it asks for during a session
Keeping AI-generated changes subject to the same CI checks and review rules as human changes
Disabling logging of the assistant's actions to protect the privacy of individual developers
Letting the assistant deploy to production on its own as soon as the test suite passes

explanation: Correct: A and C. Scaling safely means shared, reviewed configuration as the starting point and no exceptions to the existing quality gates for AI-authored work. B and E remove controls. D removes the visibility needed to operate the tooling responsibly.
